notes: Routes to care: NHS main apixaban page says 111 for symptoms of bleeding, head injury or other serious side effects (updated more recently); the side-effects page says 999/A&E for sudden severe headache, fits, vision changes, numbness. Per-symptom routing (black poo, nosebleed length) exists only in trust leaflets, which disagree with each other, so was removed. Article now states both NHS pages' wording and says they differ. Uses section now matches NHS list. Breastfeeding reason came from SPS and was dropped. Missed-dose page URL for apixaban was not retrieved; cited anticoagulants dosage page instead (6-hour rule deliberately not published). Search summaries blend pages, so URL attribution within nhs.uk/medicines/apixaban/ pages is by page title/topic, not verbatim. Doubt: one textbook sentence kept (longer clotting); NHS wording is 'blood flows more easily, less likely to clot'. Final article ~900 words incl FAQs/key facts. medications.json consistent (it also says 111/head-injury needs urgent assessment).
